newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong drops signal nine as typhoon weakening.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong drops signal nine as typhoon weakening.

text.p: Weather forecasters in Hong Kong said on Sunday they had lowered the tropical storm signal to eight from nine as Typhoon Victor weakened and moved north across the mainland.
Victor swept across the territory on Saturday, but left behind little serious damage, though one person died and more than 30 were injured.

At 2300 local time (1500 GMT) the tropical cyclone was centred about 50 km (30 miles) north-northwest of Hong Kong and was moving into mainland China at a speed of 22 km an hour (13 mph), the Hong Kong Observatory said.
Signal nine means the winds have a speed of more than 118 km per hour (73 mph).
Nearby Portuguese-ruled Macau had lowered the warning signal from nine to eight, meaning wind speeds from 63 km to 117 km per hour (40 to 73 mph).
However, heavy rains and strong winds would continue to batter the territory of 6.4 million people.
Air, land and sea traffic in both Hong Kong and Macau have ground to a halt.
